entry.title: Shifting Focus From Symptoms to Systems

media:group.media:title: Shifting Focus From Symptoms to Systems
media:group.media:description: This video public service announcement (PSA) examines the systemic barriers and their intersectionality with the social determinants of health, shaping individual experiences and outcomes. We conducted a campus-wide survey to better understand firsthand experiences and how, although these systems influence everyone, their effects are distributed unevenly.

media:group.media:description: A sense of belonging is fundamental to wellbeing, yet simply bringing people together does not guarantee meaningful connections will form. entry.title: E6 -The Conversations We Need to Have:Beyond the Clinic: Reimagining Healing Through Two-Eyed Seeing

media:group.media:title: E6 -The Conversations We Need to Have:Beyond the Clinic: Reimagining Healing Through Two-Eyed Seeing
media:group.media:description:
In this episode, we explore healing, care, and wellness through the lens of Two-Eyed Seeing—a framework that invites us to learn from both Indigenous and Western ways of knowing without positioning one above the other. Joined by Dr. Sarah Connors, an Indigenous Naturopathic Doctor, we examine how health is shaped not only by individual choices or clinical interventions, but also by relationships, community, history, culture, land, and systems. Together, we consider what it might look like for institutions to move beyond simply acknowledging diverse approaches to healing and instead create environments where Indigenous knowledge and holistic care are genuinely honoured and integrated.
Questions for reflection: 1. What assumptions about health, healing, and wellness have I inherited from the systems and institutions around me, and what perspectives might those assumptions overlook? 2. What would become possible if we approached care not as an individual responsibility alone, but as something rooted in relationships, community, culture, and connection to the land?
